title: Detect a repeat with a visited set
invariant: seen holds every value the walk has left so far. The first time x is already in seen, the walk has entered a loop.

frames.explanation: Start at x = 3. The rule is next(x) = (x·x + 1) % 10, so there are only 10 possible values and the walk must repeat eventually.
Record 3 as seen, then step: (3·3 + 1) % 10 = 0. 0 is new.
Record 0 as seen, then step: (0·0 + 1) % 10 = 1. 1 is new.
Record 1 as seen, then step: (1·1 + 1) % 10 = 2. 2 is new.
Record 2 as seen, then step: (2·2 + 1) % 10 = 5. 5 is new.
Record 5 as seen, then step: (5·5 + 1) % 10 = 6. 6 is new.
Record 6 as seen, then step: (6·6 + 1) % 10 = 7. 7 is new.
Record 7 as seen, then step: (7·7 + 1) % 10 = 0. 0 is already in the set, so the walk has come back to it.
x = 0 was seen before. The rule always sends a number to the same next number, so from here the walk repeats the same loop forever.
Start at x = 0. The rule is next(x) = (x·x + 1) % 10, so there are only 10 possible values and the walk must repeat eventually.
Record 0 as seen, then step: (0·0 + 1) % 10 = 1. 1 is new.
Record 1 as seen, then step: (1·1 + 1) % 10 = 2. 2 is new.
Record 2 as seen, then step: (2·2 + 1) % 10 = 5. 5 is new.
Record 5 as seen, then step: (5·5 + 1) % 10 = 6. 6 is new.
Record 6 as seen, then step: (6·6 + 1) % 10 = 7. 7 is new.
Record 7 as seen, then step: (7·7 + 1) % 10 = 0. 0 is already in the set, so the walk has come back to it.
x = 0 was seen before. The rule always sends a number to the same next number, so from here the walk repeats the same loop forever.
